observations: A bold white zigzag line cuts horizontally across the middle third of the image, flanked above and below by yellow sawtooth waves that run nearly edge to edge.

Upper left holds a circular form filled with red scribble lines and a large red X, set against a black disc; upper right contains a rectangular black zone with a purple oval and nested blue rectangles.
The cobalt blue background is interrupted by flat pink, black, and sky-blue shapes, with small dark red oval clusters scattered across the lower half.
reading: Two zones occupy the upper half—a scribbled circular form on the left, a boxed rectangular form on the right—held apart by a column of yellow ladder-like dashes. The white zigzag and yellow waves slice through the middle, creating a strong horizontal split. Below that line, the composition loosens into scattered ovals and open white outlines. The feeling is of high charge meeting sudden open space.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors are nnxyz nnotb #140 and nnxyz nnotb #142. Where #140 concentrates its marks in a single spiraling form on a dark ground, #141 spreads competing zones across a bright blue field—a shift from depth to flat lateral spread.

connections.reason: Both works place a red X and tight red scribble lines inside a circular form, but #140 builds those elements into a single dominant focal mass while #141 disperses them as one zone among several.

Both #141 and #142 use wide horizontal wave lines as structural dividers, but #142 shifts the ground to yellow and places a spiral form at center, whereas #141 keeps the ground blue and treats the wave as a boundary between two abstract zones.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly does the white zigzag line begin and end, and what happens to the forms directly above and below it at those edges?
ambiguities: The black rectangular zone upper-right contains layered marks that may include additional nested shapes not fully legible at this resolution.
The rawblocks #26 comparison image shows no strong formal overlap with #141 beyond shared artist; it was inspected but not selected as a connection.
